title: The Archimedean place is a blurred interval at infinity
summary: Classically, the places of $\mathbb{Q}$ are often regarded as a one-point compactification of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})$, with the real place corresponding to a formal ``prime'' added at infinity. Re-examining this picture from a topos-theoretic perspective reveals a subtler geometry: while the non-Archimedean places are identified with singletons indexed by the non-zero prime ideals of $\mathbb{Z}$, the Archimedean place is represented by the space of upper reals $\overleftarrow{[0,1]}$, which may be informally thought of as the unit interval equipped with a non-Hausdorff topology.
